prompt.context: Our client is Healthy Foods Co, a wholesaler serving a variety of clients with food products. The client is profitable but they want you to help them find revenue growth opportunities from their current business.
prompt.question: How can we help Healthy Foods Co. drive their revenue growth?

clarifying_info.a: The client serves various customer categories including independent restaurants, chain restaurants, hospitals, school cafeterias, grocery stores, and other types. Revenue by customer type is shown in Exhibit 1.

clarifying_info.q: What do customers care about most?
clarifying_info.a: Customer sensitivities ranked highest to lowest: price, convenient delivery, help with location planning, help with menu, website development, inventory, help with management optimization.
The client is one of the market leaders and is not losing market share.

exhibits.title: Total Market Revenues by Customer Type
exhibits.shows: A breakdown of revenues by customer type, listing: independent restaurants, chain restaurants, hospitals, school cafeterias, grocery stores, and other.
exhibits.data: Revenue categories: Independent restaurants, Chain restaurants, Hospitals, School cafeterias, Grocery stores, Other

exhibits.title: Client's Share of Wallet
exhibits.shows: A scatter/positional chart plotting customer size (x-axis: largest A to smallest X) against share of wallet (y-axis: 0%–70%), with labeled points A, B, C, and X, and a dividing line between 'Client is Primary food product supplier' and 'Client is one of many food product suppliers'.
exhibits.data: Y-axis: Share of Wallet 0%–70%; X-axis: Customer Size (A = largest, X = smallest); Points labeled A, B, C, X; threshold line around 40–50% share

exhibits.title: Wallet Size vs. Share of Wallet for Smaller-Revenue-Generating Customer Categories
exhibits.shows: A scatter plot with Share of Wallet (%) on the x-axis (0–60%) and Wallet Size ($M) on the y-axis (0–600), with labeled data points for Hospitals, Hotels, School cafeterias, Grocery stores, and Chain restaurants.
exhibits.data: Y-axis: Wallet Size $M (0–600); X-axis: Share of Wallet % (0–60); Hospitals: high wallet size, low share of wallet; Hotels: high wallet size, low share of wallet; School cafeterias, Grocery stores, Chain restaurants: varying positions

framework: Identify current customer mix and revenue contribution by customer type (Exhibit 1)
Analyze share of wallet by customer segment to understand penetration depth (Exhibit 2)
Prioritize growth opportunities using wallet size vs. current share of wallet framework (Exhibit 3)
Identify specific actions to capture share in high-potential segments

questions.prompt: Looking at Exhibit 1, which customer segments are most important to Healthy Foods Co. today, and what does that imply for growth strategy?
questions.guidance: Candidate should note that independent restaurants are the largest revenue contributor, with chain restaurants, hospitals, school cafeterias, grocery stores, and other segments comprising the remainder. A strong answer recognizes that the largest segment (independent restaurants) deserves scrutiny but may already be well-served.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, what does Healthy Foods Co.'s share of wallet look like across customer sizes, and what does this tell us about growth potential?
questions.guidance: Candidate should observe that for the largest customers (A, B, C), the client's share of wallet is already high — the client is the primary food product supplier. For the smallest customer (X), share is low. This means there is limited room to grow revenue from the largest customers; the opportunity lies in smaller segments where penetration is low. Candidate should articulate that growing share of wallet in large-wallet customers where penetration is low is the priority.

questions.prompt: Given that growth opportunity lies in smaller-revenue-generating customer categories, how would you prioritize which segments to target? Use Exhibit 3 to support your answer.
questions.guidance: Strong candidate frames the prioritization matrix: highest opportunity = largest wallet size AND lowest current share of wallet. Using Exhibit 3, hospitals and hotels stand out — they have large wallet sizes ($400M–$550M range) and low share of wallet (<20%), making them the most attractive targets. School cafeterias, grocery stores, and chain restaurants are lower priority due to smaller wallets or higher existing share.

math.setup: Prioritization criterion: Revenue growth potential ≈ Wallet Size × (1 − Current Share of Wallet). Hospitals and hotels have large wallets (~$400–550M) and low share (~10–15%), implying large addressable upside.
steps: Hospitals: Wallet ~$500M, share ~10% → potential upside ~$450M addressable
Hotels: Wallet ~$450M, share ~15% → potential upside ~$382M addressable
Compare to school cafeterias and grocery stores with smaller wallets or higher existing share
math.answer: Hospitals and hotels are the top-priority segments for revenue growth.

questions.prompt: How should Healthy Foods Co. increase its share of wallet in hospitals and hotels specifically?
questions.guidance: Candidate should connect back to customer sensitivities. Hospitals and hotels likely prioritize: reliable delivery (convenient delivery), inventory management (hospitals need precise supply), and potentially menu/product range help. Suggested actions: tailor delivery reliability and scheduling to hospital procurement cycles; offer inventory management support; develop specialized product lines or bundles for hotel food service; assign dedicated account managers to these segments.

brainstorming.prompt: What actions could Healthy Foods Co. take to increase its share of wallet with hospitals and hotels?

categories.name: Service & Delivery
ideas: Offer guaranteed delivery windows aligned to hospital procurement schedules
Provide just-in-time inventory replenishment to reduce storage burden
Build out dedicated delivery routes for hotel/hospital clusters

categories.name: Product & Menu
ideas: Develop specialized healthy/diet product lines tailored to hospital patient nutrition requirements
Offer seasonal or rotating menu-planning support for hotel restaurants
Bundle products into hospital-specific or hotel-specific curated packages

categories.name: Relationship & Account Management
ideas: Assign dedicated account managers to hospital and hotel accounts
Offer volume discounts or preferred pricing tiers for long-term contracts
Conduct regular business reviews to identify evolving needs

categories.name: Technology & Analytics
ideas: Provide ordering portal or app tailored to hospital/hotel procurement workflows
Share demand analytics and forecasting tools to help clients manage inventory
Integrate with existing hospital or hotel ERP/procurement systems

categories.name: Value-Added Services
ideas: Offer nutritional labeling or compliance support for hospital dietary programs
Assist with regulatory/health code compliance documentation
Provide staff training on product handling and storage for hotel kitchens

recommendation: Healthy Foods Co.'s largest near-term growth opportunity in its current business lies in increasing share of wallet with hospitals and hotels — segments with large purchasing budgets (~$400–550M wallets) where the client currently holds a small share (<20%).
The company should deprioritize further penetration of independent restaurants and other large-revenue segments where share of wallet is already high.
risks: Hospitals and hotels have complex procurement processes and long sales cycles, which may slow revenue realization
Competing for hospital/hotel business may require up-front investment in specialized delivery, service capabilities, or product lines
Existing pricing sensitivity across all segments means margin pressure if share-of-wallet gains require aggressive discounting
next_steps: Conduct detailed account-level analysis of 10–15 largest hospital and hotel prospects to quantify addressable revenue
Map current service gaps vs. hospital/hotel sensitivities (delivery reliability, inventory support) and build a targeted value proposition
Pilot a dedicated sales and service model for 2–3 anchor hospital or hotel accounts, measure share-of-wallet gains over 6 months
Scale the pilot model to broader hospital and hotel segments based on results
